Pocketwell

Coupons for the store you shop at, a shopping list that knows the price and a grocery budget on one screen, so the total you see is the total you pay. It also tracks what ten everyday staples cost near you and helps you put that in front of the people who decide.

Visit the site ↗How to useIn motion

01

Problem

Coupons, shopping lists and household budgets live in three different apps. Shoppers find out at the register what a trip really cost, cash back is counted before it arrives, and when grocery prices climb there is no simple way to show the people who decide what it costs a household.

02

What it does

Five tabs, one job each. Home shows what is left for groceries this month and the next step. Deals holds the coupons, prices and saved offers for the store you choose; every offer shows its source, size, limit, expiry and how the store applies it. List prices each item at your store with the best coupon matched and shows what is left after the trip; trip mode follows you in the aisle. Budget lets you add spending, move money or change the plan in steps, with a review before anything is saved, and explains where each number comes from. The receipt settles the numbers once, and cash back stays apart until it lands. A prices page follows ten staples month by month from official data, explains who decides each cost and drafts a letter to your representatives that you send yourself. Households share one budget with roles, and Help me save proposes changes you accept one by one.

03

How it is built

Next.js 16 and React 19 in TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Drizzle ORM on libSQL hosted by Turso, deployed on Vercel. Money is stored in whole cents, and the savings and budget math lives in pure functions that the screens and the assistant both call. Stores come from a verified list for the demo area, the Kroger API and OpenStreetMap; prices come from the Kroger API and the Bureau of Labor Statistics Average Price Data, cached so a page never waits on a provider. Each demo visitor gets a private copy of the sample household. The assistant runs through one gateway with daily spending caps and only proposes changes. 233 unit tests and 14 browser tests run on phone and computer.
